title: AI4EVER: A Graphical Deep Learning Platform For GWAS-Informed Genomic Prediction
content: Deep learning (DL) has significant potential in genomic selection (GS), but its use is constrained by the technical expertise required to design and implement neural networks. Although DL has transformed fields such as language processing and structural biology, its application in GS has not consistently outperformed traditional models such as mixed linear models. Unlocking DL's potential in GS requires exploring network architectures tailored to genomic data, a process that demands intensive programming and creates a barrier for many researchers. To overcome this challenge, we developed Artificial Intelligence for Efficient and Versatile Evaluation and Representation (AI4EVER), a freely available graphical software platform that enables users to explore and apply machine learning (ML) and DL models without coding. AI4EVER integrates a graphical user interface (GUI) with a Python-based ML backend. The platform currently supports five models: Ridge Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosted Decision Trees, Multi-Layer Perceptron, and a customizable Keras-based neural network that can predict multiple traits in a single model. A key feature of AI4EVER is the optional incorporation of genome-wide association study (GWAS) results, specifically p-values, as feature weights during model training, enabling biologically informed DL workflows. The platform also provides visualization of model performance metrics and feature-importance outputs to enhance interpretability. AI4EVER separates model training and prediction workflows, allowing trained models to be reused for independent prediction datasets. Using a representative maize dataset, we demonstrate that AI4EVER lowers the barrier to AI-enabled genomic prediction and supports data-driven decision-making in breeding programs and broader genetic improvement applications.
